text:
Sam K: Throwing up a concise follow-up from the allocator retro: propose we split responsibilities so the pool orchestrator keeps topology + global safety and a lightweight lease API handles short-lived prewarm/active windows. Trying to reduce cross-component races we keep seeing.

Sam K: High level state machine for scaler side: NONE -> REQUESTED -> PREWARM -> ACTIVE -> RELEASING. Orchestrator states: FREE -> RESERVED -> RETIRING. Events: request_lease, prewarm_ready, allocate_node, release_intent, force_revoke.

Lina T: Love it. Quick clarifying Qs: 1) Who responds to an urgent preemption conflict if two tenants request last headroom GPU? 2) What metrics should trigger request_lease vs direct activation?

Sam K: 1) Orchestrator makes the final call (global fairness). Scaler can set preempt_priority on RequestLease but orch keeps policy enforcement. 2) RequestLease is used when 95p tail latency exceeds threshold OR sustained token rate increase over baseline. Direct activation only if the tenant already holds warm resources.

Diego R: Suggest adding an admission_status enum returned by orch: {OK, SOFT_THROTTLE, QUEUE_BURST, DENIED}. Include reason code so scaler can fallback to smaller model or reduce batch size.

Sam K: Yep. Reason strings like "headroom_low", "preemption_window", "quota_limit". Scaler should have hooks: fallback_model(), reduce_batch(), client_queue().

Maya P: Observability note: we need a single lease_correlation_id and timestamps: req_ts, grant_ts, prewarm_done_ts, active_ts, release_ts, revoke_ts. Also include lease.owner, lease.priority, and decision_rationale short text.

Lina T: +1 on rationale. Keep it capped (200-256 chars). Also include orch node_id assigned so we can map GPU telemetry.

Sam K: Edge case: draining while an ACTIVE lease still holds KV cache. Proposal: scaler sends Release(lease_id, expected_shutdown_ts). Orch replies {ACK, ACK_WITH_GRACE_MS, FORCE_REVOKE}. FORCE_REVOKE triggers KV eviction metrics and a forced fallback route. Max_grace configurable per-tenant.

Diego R: For backpressure, make probe->prewarm cooldown per-tenant (default 45s) and exponential backoff on repeated failed prewarms. Avoid noisy oscillation.

Sam K: Agreed. Add probe_cooldown_seconds and failed_prewarm_backoff_ms in config.

Lina T: Can we sketch a minimal RPC surface? My draft: 
```
RequestLease(tenant_id, demand_estimate, preempt_priority) -> {status, lease_id, ttl_ms, admission_status, decision_rationale, assigned_node}
KeepAlive(lease_id) -> {status, new_ttl_ms}
Release(lease_id, expected_release_ts) -> {status, grace_ms}
OrchEvents(stream) -> {lease_granted, lease_revoked, headroom_update, preemption_notice}
```

Maya P: Also emit billing_tag on grant so cost attribution for prewarm time is straightforward. That helps reconcile prewarm amortization.

orch-bot: autoscaler-staging: canary deploy of "lease-api" branch succeeded :white_check_mark:

Diego R: Simulation ask: I'll run a contested-headroom sim that mixes reserved-credit tenants and burst tenants, measure fairness and latency regressions.

Maya P: I'll add Console panels showing lease phase durations and a flamechart mapping where time is spent across grant->prewarm->active. Also surface decision_rationale in the trace.

Sam K: Next steps: I'll add a protobuf sketch + state diagrams to the RFC, include the config knobs and the admission_status codes. Lina, can you write a tiny unit test harness that fuzzes conflicting RequestLease calls? Diego, run the sims next week. Maya, wire the mock traces. Target RFC ack by EOW. Thanks! :thumbsup:
